origin: Own centered Gaussian scientific-signal model comparison with exact sufficient statistics. The datasets are constructed mathematical summaries with known independent noise variance1 and sample mean0; they do not represent a measured named experiment. All priors below are PROPER normalized densities. Likelihood constants shared by models cancel only after the ratio is defined.
models_and_observations: For each N in[16,256,4096,65536], independent observations obeyY_i|beta~Normal(beta,1), with observedsumY_i=0. The residual sum of squares is the same for all compared models and irrelevant to their relative evidence. DefineL_N(beta)/L_N(0)=exp(-N*beta²/2). ModelM0fixesbeta0. ModelM1usesbeta~Normal(0,1). ModelM2setsbeta=u*v with independentu,v~Normal(0,1). All three prior model probabilities are1/3. Forj1,2defineZ_j(N)=integral[L_N(beta)/L_N(0)]dPi_j, soZ0=1. These are RELATIVE marginal likelihoods against the fixed null likelihood, not normalized probabilities over N and not absolute data densities. M1andM2 may have the same set of possible means while their induced prior measures differ.
evidence_and_singular_geometry: ComputeZ1,Z2, Bayes factorZ2/Z1and posterior model weights(M0,M1,M2)for everyN. Derive the exact one-dimensional integral after integrating out one M2factor and explain the entire likelihood maximizer setuv0. Assess whether an ordinary two-parameter Laplace/Hessian/BIC penalty is valid; do not repair a singularity by silently fixing a nuisance factor or choosing one point on a likelihood ridge. Derive the leading large-Nform logZ=-lambda*logN+(m-1)*loglogN+O(1)for each nonnullmodel, report the coefficientslambdaandm-1, and determinelim sqrt(N)*Z2(N)/logN. Compare the naive total-parameter BIC pairwise factor usingd1=1,d2=2with exact Bayes factors. A pairwise preference between two nonnull parametrizations must not be confused with evidence against the fixed null model. The asymptotic statement is for this observed zero-mean sequence, not a generic unknown true-parameter theorem.
posterior_and_prediction: UnderM2derive the posterior variance and standardized excess kurtosis E[beta^4|data]/Var(beta|data)^2-3, plus the exact model-conditional posterior predictiveP(|Y_new|>2)and predictive density atY_new0for everyN. Y_newhas independent unit Gaussian observation noise conditional on the SAME underlying beta. Compare each exact mixture tail with a centered Gaussian of matching predictive variance1+Var(beta|data), and determine whether either the beta posterior or the predictive law is exactlyGaussian. The standardized four-moment summary and finite-tail comparison test distributional shape across sample sizes; matching a variance alone does not establish a Gaussian law. Check the zero predictive density through sequential evidence updatingZ2(N+1)/(sqrt(2pi)*Z2(N)); adding a future observation0updatesboth Nand the sufficient statistic appropriately.
normal_mixture_and_accuracy: A convenient deterministic route integrates outv and then changes u=sinh(t)/sqrt(N). Derive the correct normalization/measure yourself, including its Jacobian. Conditional on u and thezero-mean data, beta is centered Gaussian with varianceu²/(1+Nu²), and predictiveY_newis Gaussian with variance1+that quantity; the posterior mixing density foru is not its prior. Use actual registered normal-distribution outputs for the complete component Gaussian tail values used in the predictive integral, preserving operation/input/output order and logs if returned. All evidence, posterior and mixture integrals need numerical convergence and a quantified tail/truncation argument; naive plug-in probabilities, an arbitrary cutoff or unassessed Monte Carlo errors are insufficient. The public numerical appendix supplies optional generic32and64LegendreJacobi matrices; if used, retain complete registered symmetric spectral outputs, actual nodes/weights and their normalization, and actual weighted matrix products for the reported integrals. You may derive and validate another deterministic numerical or analytic integration route; no particular code or special-function library is required. A continuous symbolic/asymptotic proof cannot be replaced by fitting a line to four Nvalues.
prior_measure_and_reparameterization: ForM1definegamma=2betaand write the same likelihood asNormal(gamma/2,1). Derive the transformed normalized prior density ongammaand decide whether a correct variable change altersZ1. Separately consider a NEW proper priorgamma~Normal(0,1); compute its relative evidence divided by originalZ1for everyNand explain why this is a changed model/prior rather than a coordinate dependence of Bayes theorem. Finally suppose one rewrites the original kernel asphi(gamma/2)but omits ONLY the change-of-variable density factor, retaining the same likelihood and kernel. Report that unnormalized prior integral and its spurious marginal-evidence multiplier. Distinguish this missing-normalization mistake from deliberately assigning a different proper prior.

interpretation_proposals.A: Parameter counting alone need not give the marginal-likelihood penalty at a singular, nonidentifiable likelihood maximum.
interpretation_proposals.B: Two parametrizations spanning the same mean family necessarily induce the same prior predictive distribution under unrelated unit normal parameter priors.
interpretation_proposals.C: A correctly transformed prior measure preserves evidence, whereas changing the prior or dropping its Jacobian need not.
interpretation_proposals.D: The larger M2versusM1Bayes factor proves a nonzero signal even if the null model retains greater posterior weight.
interpretation_proposals.E: A Gaussian mixture can match a Gaussian variance while retaining a nonzero fourth cumulant and different predictive tails.
interpretation_proposals.F: A good straight-line fit in logNto four evidence values proves the absence of a loglogNterm.
interpretation_proposals.G: Conditioning on data leaves the mixing variable prior unchanged when the likelihood depends on the productuv.
interpretation_proposals.H: Model comparison, likelihood-family expressiveness, prior concentration and predictive shape answer different scientific questions.

Signal moments, predictive probabilities and density values retain their own units; densities are not event probabilities. The loglogNcoefficient field ism-1in the stated sign convention, notm. All boolean, multiplicity/coefficient and interpretation distinctions remain scientific requirements.
